topic: Why an AI watermark remover hit 11k stars
angle: A tool this popular is a signal about what users think of the labels
hook: An AI watermark remover just hit 11,000 stars
caption:
A tool whose entire purpose is stripping AI watermarks passed eleven thousand GitHub stars. Set aside whether that is good — as a signal it is unambiguous. The labelling approach the whole industry agreed on is being actively removed by the people it was applied to.

slides.text: An AI watermark remover just hit *11,000* stars
slides.subline: That number is telling you something

slides.text: Eleven thousand people starred a tool that exists to delete the label the industry agreed to add.

slides.title: Why people want it gone
slides.body: The visible watermark marks the output as lesser regardless of how much work went into it. People who spent a day directing a result object to being flagged the same as a one-line prompt.

slides.caption: on a tool built purely to strip AI content labels

slides.left_text: Label AI output so people can tell what they are looking at.
slides.right_text: A popular tool for removing the label, and invisible marking instead.

slides.title: What this means for you
slides.body: Visible watermarks are on the way out and invisible provenance is replacing them. If you publish AI-assisted work, assume it is detectable whether or not you can see a mark on it.
